title: Microburst tail-latency & memory-pressure sweep for FP8/INT8 variants with KV-cache warmup
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: quantify tail-latency and throughput degradation modes for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants when exposed to microburst traffic and long-context KV-cache dynamics across mixed batch sizes. This ticket defines a benchmark matrix, calibration and accuracy validation steps, and an orchestration plan to reproduce and measure kernel-fallbacks and memory-pressure effects that cause SLO regressions. Outcome: actionable knobs (batching caps, KV-cache warmup thresholds, kernel-fallback policies) and a gated regression threshold for CI/rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro script + CI job that runs the full matrix and emits p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tail throughput, and delta in per-token log-prob against fp32 baseline. 2) Calibration artifacts for FP8/INT8 variants saved and validated on holdout prompt set (human-curated long-context set). 3) Documented thresholds for automatic kernel-fallback and memory fallbacks with recommended defaults. 4) A short runbook section describing mitigation steps when microburst-induced tail latency > 2x baseline or quality drop > 0.6% absolute (or configurable).
benchmark_matrix: Dimensions: model (redwood-7b variant), precision (fp32 baseline, fp8-ef4-profile, int8-symmetric-profile), batch sizes [1,4,8,16], request mix [steady, microburst(10x spike over 5s), mixed long/short], context lengths [512, 2048, 8192]. Cross with KV-cache state: cold (first request), warm (after 20 warmup tokens), stale (KV partially evicted). Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), memory high-water, kernel-fallback count, CPU/GPU utilization, per-token log-prob delta, exact-match on structured outputs for eval prompts.
calibration_workflow: 1) Create calibration runner that produces INT8/FP8 scale tables using representative corpus with long-context sequences (mix of doc-length and interactive chat traces). 2) Persist calibration artifacts to s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/{run_id}/ and register in model-catalog. 3) Validate calibration by running 1000 holdout prompts and comparing log-prob delta vs fp32; if median delta > 0.4% or max delta > 2% mark as failed. 4) Generate summary CSV with per-layer sensitivity and suggested per-layer override list.
accuracy_validation: Holdout sets: (a) conversational long-flow (200 prompts, avg 2500 tokens), (b) code completion snippets (500 prompts), (c) structured-output templates (100 prompts). Metrics: delta perplexity, average per-token log-prob change, structured-output exact-match, human-eval pass-rate on 50 critical prompts. Thresholds: median log-prob delta <= 0.4% for pass; any regression leading to >0.6% user-visible failure requires rollback. All validation must attach the calibration artifact id used.
orchestration_plan: Implement a bench-orchestrator workflow (GH Actions + internal runner) that: spins up dedicated test cluster (runtime-1.26 image), deploys model variants with pinned calibration artifacts, replays traffic patterns using loadgenerator v2, collects telemetry to observability dashboard (dashboards/quant-microburst-ENG-135432). The CI job should run nightly on PRs touching quant calibration or kernel selection codepaths.
runbook_mitigation: If microburst tail or p99 jumps > 2x baseline: 1) reduce max batch window to next lower setting, 2) enable conservative kernel-fallback thresholds (force fp32 path for offending layers), 3) pre-warm KV-cache by issuing synthetic prefetch requests on blackbox upgrade, 4) escalate to runtime on-call and attach latest dashboard snapshot.
steps: Design full matrix and implement bench-orchestrator job
Add calibration runner support for per-layer override hints
Create holdout prompt sets and upload to s3
Run smoke tests on small cluster to validate telemetry and artifact registration
Execute full sweep across precisions and collect metrics
Analyze tail-latency clusters and produce recommendations
Write PR with defaults and runtime flags to gate aggressive quant rollout

2026-02-24 - SRE (Riley Park): Observed GPU memory high-water events when batch size 16 + context 8192 on INT8 profile; suggested adding kernel-fallback counters to telemetry.

2026-02-28 - Aisha Kapoor: Added per-layer override plan; calibration runner now emits per-layer sensitivity CSV. Initial accuracy validation: fp8 median log-prob delta 0.32% vs fp32 baseline; INT8 shows a few layers with >1.5% delta on code-completion subset.
2026-03-03 - Mateo Chen: Full sweep run queued; artifact manifest at s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/ENG-135432/manifest.csv. Benchmarks will populate dashboards overnight.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Kapoor: Preliminary results in dashboard: FP8 gives stable throughput gains but microburst p99 increases ~2.4x for warmed KV-cache + batch>=8 on 8192 context. Decided to implement conservative default that caps burst-batching for long-context for FP8. Next: propose runtime flag and CI gate.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive batching increases amortized cost but worsens p99 during microbursts due to KV-cache alignment and kernel scheduling contention. INT8 provides most cost savings but requires per-layer overrides for code-heavy workloads. Plan to ship conservative defaults and allow per-customer tuning via Dedicated/Private configs.
